raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-ALB-CitizenServiceDelivery",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Construction of the new Citizen Service Center facility in Tirana could generate localized environmental impacts such as dust, noise, waste generation, traffic disruption, and safety hazards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate the site-specific Environmental Management Plan (EMP) into bidding documents and construction contracts, ensure supervisor monitoring, and comply with Albanian construction permitting laws.",
      "evidence": "Operational policy OP 4.01 is triggered and the project categorized as a World Bank Category B because a new building will be constructed for CSC"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "ADISA is a newly established agency with limited implementation track record and weak procurement/fiduciary capacity, risking project execution delays and non-compliance with World Bank guidelines.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated PMU within ADISA staffed with qualified procurement and FM specialists, provide continuous World Bank fiduciary training, and utilize MoF's CFCU during the PPF phase.",
      "evidence": "Created in October 2014, ADISA has a limited track record of implementation experience, but some members of the project team have relevant experience."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Civil servants and participating line agencies may resist ceding front-office service delivery to ADISA/CSCs, potentially undermining business process re-engineering and service integration.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement a structured change management and outreach program, engage agency reform champions, and establish clear communications to align civil service incentives with new service standards.",
      "evidence": "Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back-office functions."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Heavy emphasis on online service delivery and high-end urban Citizen Service Centers risks excluding poor, rural, elderly, and marginalized populations with low digital literacy or access.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Maintain alternative physical access points, establish assisted digital access network points (e.g., at local government centers and internet cafes), offer call center helplines, and conduct targeted outreach.",
      "evidence": "there is a risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "High operational complexity and inter-sectoral coordination requirements across more than ten participating ministries and agencies could cause decision-making bottlenecks and implementation delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Maintain strong oversight through the Prime Minister-led Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee, Technical Inter-Ministerial Committee, and active progress monitoring and barrier-unblocking by the Delivery Unit.",
      "evidence": "Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "An ambitious and compressed reform timeline for process re-engineering, legislative updates, and service automation may result in missed target dates and delayed disbursements under the results-based loan.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Balance quick-win interventions with long-term structural reforms, structure results-based financing across a 5-year timeline, and provide just-in-time technical assistance to participating agencies.",
      "evidence": "The Government’s timeline for the reform is very ambitious."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Manual payroll processes and unintegrated accounting systems across participating budgetary and non-budgetary agencies create financial management control risks in Eligible Expenditure Programs (EEPs).",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Adopt a comprehensive Financial Management Manual, recruit qualified PMU finance specialists, procure dedicated project accounting software, and conduct annual High State Control audits of EEPs.",
      "evidence": "The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Incomplete digitization, missing National ID records, and unresolved legal ownership issues in legacy state databases (e.g., IPRO) could hinder backend system integration and automation.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide targeted technical assistance and financing to digitize legacy paper records, clean up data, link National IDs, and integrate agency databases with NAIS's government interoperability platform.",
      "evidence": "The National ID number is missing for most records, only 45 to 50 percent of the archive is digitized, and legal issues over ownership remain"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Discrepancies between official internal administrative processing logs and actual citizen transaction times could result in inaccurate baseline assessment and unreliable performance monitoring.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Utilize independent bi-annual user surveys, deploy third-party validation (TPV) for DLI achievements, and implement proactive SMS citizen feedback mechanisms to capture real user experience.",
      "evidence": "This anomaly could be the result of poor reporting of data or poor definition of the process."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Delays in drafting and parliamentary approval of mandatory omnibus primary legislation and secondary bylaws could halt the legal enactment of re-engineered business processes.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Mobilize ministerial working groups overseen by the Technical Inter-Ministerial Committee to prepare legal inventories early and engage legal consultants under TA to draft the omnibus bill.",
      "evidence": "Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Inadequate long-term budget allocations for ongoing ICT software licensing, hardware maintenance, and periodic upgrades could compromise the operational sustainability of digitized services.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Detail full lifecycle recurrent cost requirements in the approved Reform Policy Document, secure explicit government budget commitments, and explore public-private partnership (PPP) operational models.",
      "evidence": "Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance. To continue efficiency improvements once services have been automated, the Government will have to upgrade periodically."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Strong dependence on top-level political leadership creates vulnerability if cabinet turnover or shifting political priorities erode institutional support for service delivery reforms.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Institutionalize reform mandates within permanent structures (ADISA, NAIS, Delivery Unit), anchor financial support to five-year DLIs, and generate public demand via open citizen feedback reporting.",
      "evidence": "There is high level political commitment and push, which is a great asset to the project. The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk"
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Construction of the new Citizen Service Center facility in Tirana could generate localized environmental impacts such as dust, noise, waste generation, traffic disruption, and safety hazards.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate the site-specific Environmental Management Plan (EMP) into bidding documents and construction contracts, ensure supervisor monitoring, and comply with Albanian construction permitting laws.
risks.evidence: Operational policy OP 4.01 is triggered and the project categorized as a World Bank Category B because a new building will be constructed for CSC

risks.description: ADISA is a newly established agency with limited implementation track record and weak procurement/fiduciary capacity, risking project execution delays and non-compliance with World Bank guidelines.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated PMU within ADISA staffed with qualified procurement and FM specialists, provide continuous World Bank fiduciary training, and utilize MoF's CFCU during the PPF phase.
risks.evidence: Created in October 2014, ADISA has a limited track record of implementation experience, but some members of the project team have relevant experience.

risks.description: Civil servants and participating line agencies may resist ceding front-office service delivery to ADISA/CSCs, potentially undermining business process re-engineering and service integration.
risks.mitigation: Implement a structured change management and outreach program, engage agency reform champions, and establish clear communications to align civil service incentives with new service standards.
risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back-office functions.

risks.description: Heavy emphasis on online service delivery and high-end urban Citizen Service Centers risks excluding poor, rural, elderly, and marginalized populations with low digital literacy or access.
risks.mitigation: Maintain alternative physical access points, establish assisted digital access network points (e.g., at local government centers and internet cafes), offer call center helplines, and conduct targeted outreach.
risks.evidence: there is a risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access

risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

risks.description: An ambitious and compressed reform timeline for process re-engineering, legislative updates, and service automation may result in missed target dates and delayed disbursements under the results-based loan.
risks.mitigation: Balance quick-win interventions with long-term structural reforms, structure results-based financing across a 5-year timeline, and provide just-in-time technical assistance to participating agencies.

risks.mitigation: Mobilize ministerial working groups overseen by the Technical Inter-Ministerial Committee to prepare legal inventories early and engage legal consultants under TA to draft the omnibus bill.
risks.evidence: Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016.

risks.description: Inadequate long-term budget allocations for ongoing ICT software licensing, hardware maintenance, and periodic upgrades could compromise the operational sustainability of digitized services.
risks.mitigation: Detail full lifecycle recurrent cost requirements in the approved Reform Policy Document, secure explicit government budget commitments, and explore public-private partnership (PPP) operational models.
